text:
Bitcoin retraced to the $62,600–$62,900 range on Tuesday, July 8, as U.S.-Iran geopolitical escalation pushed Brent crude above $76/bbl and revived inflation fears. The risk-off shift weighed on digital assets and global equities simultaneously, with the Nasdaq facing renewed selling pressure as markets question the AI-led rally's sustainability. Despite the pullback, spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $21.4 million in net inflows — their third consecutive positive day — signaling that institutional re-entry remains intact.

The FOMC minutes from the June 16–17 meeting release today are the primary macro event. Markets are pricing in a ~50% probability of a September rate adjustment under Chair Kevin Warsh. The DXY held above 101 on safe-haven demand, while 10-year Treasury yields climbed on oil-driven inflation expectations. Rising yields and a stronger dollar historically compress crypto risk premiums, making today's FOMC minutes a critical catalyst for near-term digital asset direction.
